Als er Herrn von Holstein nannte, einen der wichtigsten Mitarbeiter des Fürsten, schien mir, dass eine leichte Warnung vor diesem Mann in den Worten des Fürsten mitschwang. Nachdem er ihnen zugehört hatte, stand der Fürst auf und entgegnete: Jetzt lenke ich Europa im Vierspänner! Nach Ansicht des genannten Herrn lag der Fürst damit falsch, denn schon damals drohte eine russisch-französische Freundschaft anstelle der russisch-preußischen, mit anderen Worten, zwei Pferde waren bereits aus dem Vierspänner auszuschließen.

L'idée était que les colonies seraient défendues depuis chez nous. À mon retour, tant MON GRAND-PÈRE que le Prince m'ont loué pour mon rapport clair et honnête, ce qui m'a fait plaisir car je ressentais la lourde impression d'avoir dû désillusionner ces hautes personnalités sur plusieurs points. Selon la Russie, la diplomatie de Disraeli avait transformé l'œuvre honnête de Bismarck en une négociation pour une victoire anglo-autrichienne contre la Russie. Sur ce, il quitta la pièce. Ensuite, le Prince voulut rédiger un texte de réponse à la Reine. C'était particulièrement vrai en ce qui concerne un système industriel comme celui de la Belgique, qui pouvait, sans entrave, extraire la dernière goutte des réserves humaines belges et payer des salaires très bas, sans éprouver de remords ni de compassion pour le moral en déclin de ce peuple épuisé et sans protection. Je rendais souvent visite au Prince ainsi qu'au comte Herbert. L'HOMME AUX YEUX DE HYÈNE. Lorsque je suis devenu plus intime avec le cercle de Bismarck, j'ai entendu des discours plus ouverts sur Herr von Holstein. Il était en contact avec beaucoup d'hommes, de toutes classes sociales et milieux, par tous il était révéré et estimé, et j'ai moi aussi traité avec amitié et gratitude. Ceux qui en faisaient partie, bien qu'ignorant mes pensées et objectifs profonds, adoptèrent une attitude méfiante et réservée envers moi, au lieu de transférer leur intérêt du père au fils, afin de favoriser le bien-être de la patrie.

From that day forward, my interactions with the Queen, who was even feared by her own children, were of the best possible nature; from then on, she addressed her grandson solely as a sovereign equal to herself. On my initial travels, Count Herbert accompanied me as the Foreign Office’s representative. What he desired was fulfilled. In fulfilling my duty during this crisis, I vigilantly observed all developments in military, official, and social domains, and felt deep indignation at the widespread signs of negligence, particularly the increasing hostility directed at my mother. The assembly resumed its work, producing abundant material for expanding the social laws initiated by Emperor William the Great, which are Germany’s pride, demonstrating protection of the working classes unmatched anywhere else. Yet this proved hardly feasible as long as Prince Bismarck remained in office, since he claimed the chief decision-making role in all matters, thus limiting the independence of his collaborators. Encouraged by the compelling speeches of Achenbach, I developed a special interest in the economic progress of the nation’s internal development, while the judicial administration caught my interest less. This was inevitable. Governmental protection on one side, and the iron fist on the other comprised Bismarck’s social policy. As my duty dictated, I informed the Prince that merchants and capitalists were vigorously expanding the colonies, and according to Hanseatic sources, they expected naval protection. This was particularly evident when the Count asked to leave concurrently with his father’s retirement. Later, I frequently discussed colonial issues with the Prince and consistently found he intended to use the colonies as commercial assets or bargaining chips rather than to benefit the fatherland or exploit raw material sources. For that reason, I stressed the urgent need to build a fleet in time, so German possessions abroad would not remain unprotected; since the Prince had hoisted the German flag overseas and the people supported it, a navy must also back it. However, the Prince ignored my statements, relying on his favorite motto: If the English landed on our soil, I would have them arrested. His belief was that colonies would be defended domestically. He was fundamentally conservative but had to balance this with openness and avoid narrow-mindedness and prejudice against other factions. Bennigsen agreed with me when I told him the National Liberals should revise their program, which originally, under the slogan Maintenance of the German Empire and Freedom of the Press, had long united members under the Liberal flag, so that through revision the influential appeal of old Prussian Liberalism would not diminish among the people. Yet, I always kept my distance. Later, when I told a gentleman at the Foreign Office about this, he said he had been present when the Prince, after signing the Berlin Treaty, entered the Foreign Office and was congratulated by the assembled officials. On the contrary! He was too great a statesman to underestimate the labor issue’s importance to the state. Petersburg marked my first political act before the world’s eyes, underscoring our ties to Russia according to my late grandfather’s last wish. He has ruined the old friendship between us, planted distrust within the Court and Government, and stirred the notion of a grave injustice against the Russian army following its arduous campaign, which fuels its desire for revenge.

During the ninety-nine days when I was still Crown Prince, I quietly considered those individuals I intended to appoint later, as the doctors left no doubt that my father's time was limited. Bennigsen made a striking observation, warning that if the North German Liberals fell under the influence of the South German Democrats, genuine Liberalism would vanish, replaced by a disguised democracy emerging from below, which was unwelcome here. The Conservative party, loyal and honorable to its King, unfortunately did not always produce leaders of exceptional talent who were also skilled, tactically adept politicians. Bismarck remained steadfast; he insisted he would take responsibility for his decisions and that all I needed to do was entrust the matter to him. Additionally, I was deeply pained by the ongoing smear campaigns portraying me as estranged from my father. AFTER BECOMING EMPEROR Following Emperor Frederick III's passing, the heavy responsibility of ruling the Empire rested on my young shoulders. The assembly resumed its work, producing an abundance of material to expand the social legislation initiated by Emperor William the Great, a source of pride for Germany as it demonstrated a protective stance toward the working classes unmatched anywhere else. Two journalists were particularly active in this effort: one Herr Schnidrowitz and MHis broad talents had made him known as Court Marshal throughout Europe, and equally capable as an ambassador or Imperial Chancellor! Had he informed England of his proposal to the Tsar? I earned the Prince's confidence, who consulted me on many matters. During a conversation with one about relations between the two courts, armies, and nations—relations I found were evolving compared to earlier times—the old General remarked, 'C'est ce vilain congrès de Berlin.' The General noticed His Majesty was deeply agitated after speaking with Bismarck, fearing for the old Emperor’s health, advising him to avoid such distress in the future; and that if Bismarck refused to obey His Majesty’s wishes, he should be dismissed. A certain clause had to be moderated to preserve the law, which Bismarck opposed. Dutifully, I pointed out to the Prince that merchants and capitalists were energetically developing the colonies and, as I learned from Hanseatic circles, expected naval protection. He offered me many valuable pieces of advice for the future, drawn from his devoted, genuinely Prussian heart firmly loyal to the sovereign's family, yet tolerant of other parties. HANDLING A COAL STRIKE The major Westphalian coal workers' strike in spring took the civil administration by surprise, causing confusion and dismay, especially among Westphalian officials. HIS GRANDFATHER'S SUCCESSOR The tragic aspect for me regarding Bismarck was that I became my grandfather's successor—that is, in a way, I skipped a generation.

body: He quickly earned widespread respect and affection among the workers, managing them so effectively that complete calm prevailed throughout his jurisdiction. He pleased his son by inscribing on a small card his gratitude for THE KAISER'S MEMOIRS, expressing the honor he felt at observing these troops and his pride in calling them his own. This brought me great joy and fulfilled my entire existence. The Prince, present during the final hours of the old Emperor and privy to his political testament to his grandson—particularly regarding the special attention to be given to relations with Russia—prompted my summer journey to St. The prognosis of the treacherous illness that claimed Emperor Frederick III was frankly disclosed to me beforehand by German doctors summoned as experts by the English physician Sir Morell Mackenzie. Tu peux te fier a moi* I documented this significant conversation immediately when it took place. Still, this dispute over political strategies cannot diminish my esteem for Bismarck's stature as a statesman; he remains the architect of the German Empire, and surely no individual has done more for his nation. Since the vital issue of unifying the Empire was always foremost in my mind, I refrained from being swayed by the agitations common in those times. When nervous and troubling telegrams from leading industrialists and officials reached the Imperial Chancellor's office, I asked Michaelis about the situation; he replied via telegram that everything was calm except among Government officials. Throughout spring and summer, extensive material was gathered from announcements and reports revealing that all was not well in industrial circles; many of the workers’ demands were justified and deserved sympathetic consideration by both employers and officials. These two men, both seasoned military officers with firm principles, shared their master's sentiments and remained loyally devoted to me until their deaths. I appointed General von Wittich as my First Adjutant General and General von Hahnke, commander of the Second Infantry Guard Division, as chief of my Military Cabinet. The latter was a close friend of Emperor Frederick III and had been my brigade commander when I served with the First Infantry Guard Regiment. This situation alone sufficed, as a Premier of such overwhelming significance, who had secured great political triumphs for Prussia and Germany, completely dominated his Ministers and ruled them despotically. For that reason, while Prince of Prussia, I avoided any attempts to involve me in party politics. At that early time, my attention was drawn to our reliance on England, given our lack of a navy and English control of Heligoland. PROPHECY OF RUSSIAN DOWNFALL At Brest-Litovsk, amid constant military preparations, I noticed that the demeanor of Russian officers toward me was distinctly cooler and more aloof than during my first visit to St. HANDLING A COAL STRIKE The major Westphalian coal miners’ strike in spring caught the civil administration off guard, causing considerable confusion, especially among Westphalian administrative members. My parents disapproved of Prince Bismarck and viewed unfavorably their son's involvement in the Prince's circle. The commanders of the summoned troops reported on the situation as encountered, including one of my former barrack comrades, Michaelis of the Hussar Guard Regiment, known for his wit. He rode alone, unarmed, among the striking workers camped on the warm hillsides and soon established harmless communication with them through his approachable and cheerful demeanor. The military entourages of the two emperors and the officialdom had grown too old. He rapidly gained general appreciation and affection from the workers, managing them so well that complete peace prevailed in his region. I soon realized that the Ministers, fully under Bismarck's control, could not support reforms or ideas of the young master that Bismarck opposed. Regarding his prudence and skill, Emperor William the Great once remarked pointedly to von Albedyll, his chief of Cabinet. This state of affairs alone was sufficient, as a Premier of such immense importance, who had achieved great political victories for Prussia and Germany, completely dominated his Ministers and ruled them despotically. The General found His Majesty highly agitated after a discussion with Bismarck, fearing for the old Emperor’s health. He advised His Majesty to avoid such worries in the future, suggesting that if Bismarck refused to act according to His Majesty's wishes, he should be dismissed. I heard he was very shrewd, diligent, excessively proud, a peculiar man who avoided public appearances and social contacts, full of suspicion, prone to whims, and, beyond all, a fierce enemy, thus dangerous. From every direction came demands for troops; every mine owner wished to have guards stationed outside their premises. Prince Bismarck opposed this as well. To encourage them, I allowed them free rein in their respective domains. GERMANY AS PEACEMAKER It must also be emphasized that it was a German statesman who, in , averted a general war, even at the expense of straining Germany's relations with Russia, believing rightly that he would eventually strengthen those ties again or at least prevent conflicts after overcoming the crisis threatening Europe. I had studied enough history to protect myself from the illusion of thinking it possible to satisfy an entire people. This contrasted with the General Staff under Moltke. This realization was confirmed when I questioned my former private teacher, Privy Councilor Dr. I earned the Prince's trust, who consulted me on many matters. The Tsar received me warmly at Brest-Litovsk, and I attended troop reviews and fortress and defensive maneuvers that, even then, clearly had an anti-German character. When the Prince decided to present his offer to the Tsar, he must have revised his political views that had led to San Stefano and the Congress of Berlin; or, due to the evolving political situation in Europe, he deemed it time to reshuffle the political cards differently, or as my grandfather put it, to juggle them anew. A few years before the war, people in England, pressured by labor troubles, realized the necessity of better care for workers.

Gradually, I realized I effectively lacked control over a Ministry of State; those composing it, through long habit, saw themselves as Prince Bismarck’s officials. Upon inquiry as to why the Prince held such a negative view, he explained that Count Herbert had given an unfavorable report on Turkey. When I asked the Prince why he held this adverse opinion, he replied that Count Herbert’s critical report on Turkey was the cause. Au moment où il refusait de suivre tes instructions, il allait être renvoyé. Lorsque j'ai présenté cette lettre au Prince, il a cédé à une violente colère. C’est là que réside la faiblesse dans la supériorité des grands hommes. Même le Congrès de Berlin en 1878, à mon avis, fut une erreur, tout comme le Kulturkampf. De plus, la constitution de l'Empire fut élaborée pour s'adapter à la prépondérance extraordinaire de Bismarck en tant qu’homme d'État ; les grandes bottes de cuirassier ne convenaient pas à tout le monde. C’est pourquoi j’ai souligné qu’il fallait prendre des mesures pour construire une flotte à temps, afin que les biens allemands à l’étranger ne soient pas sans défense ; puisque le Prince avait hissé le drapeau allemand hors du pays, et que le peuple le soutenait, il devait aussi y avoir une marine pour le protéger.

LES POSSESSIONS CONTINENTALES DE BISMARCK Mais le Prince est resté sourd à mes remarques et s’en est tenu à sa devise favorite : si les Anglais devaient débarquer sur notre sol, je les ferais arrêter. Son idée était que les colonies seraient défendues depuis la métropole. Au retour, tant mon grand-père que le Prince m’ont félicité pour mon rapport clair et direct, ce qui me plaisait d’autant plus que je me sentais oppressé par le fait d’avoir dû décevoir ces hautes personnalités sur plusieurs points. Pour la Russie, la politique de Disraeli avait transformé l’œuvre honnête de Bismarck en une négociation d’une victoire anglo-autrichienne contre la Russie.

Ainsi, le Ministère des Affaires étrangères n'était rien d'autre qu'un bureau du grand Chancelier, où les tâches étaient accomplies selon ses directives. J’ai ajouté que, autrement, j’étais son petit-fils aimant, toujours reconnaissant de tout conseil venant de ma grand-mère, qui avait accumulé tant d'expérience durant son long règne ; cependant, dans les affaires concernant l'Allemagne, je me devais de conserver ma liberté d'action ; la visite à Saint-Pétersbourg était prévue. Elle disait qu’il fallait d’abord respecter une année de deuil, puis ma première visite devait lui être dédiée, puisqu’elle était ma grand-mère, ainsi qu’à l’Angleterre, terre natale de ma mère, avant de considérer d’autres pays.

Alors, il quitta la pièce. Le Prince souhaita rédiger une réponse à la Reine. Cela était particulièrement vrai en ce qui concerne un système industriel comme celui de la Belgique, capable d'exploiter sans entrave toutes les réserves humaines de la Belgique, offrant de bas salaires, sans ressentir la moindre conscience ni compassion pour le moral en déclin du peuple épuisé et sans protection.

Je rendais souvent visite au Prince ainsi qu’au Comte Herbert. L’HOMME AUX YEUX DE HYÈNE. En devenant plus proche du cercle de Bismarck, j’entendais des discours plus francs sur Herr von Holstein. Il était en contact avec de nombreuses personnes, de toutes classes sociales et professions, qui le respectaient et l’estimaient, tout comme moi, avec amitié et reconnaissance. Ceux qui y appartenaient, bien qu’ignorant mes pensées et objectifs intérieurs, adoptaient une attitude méfiante et réservée à mon égard, au lieu de transférer leur intérêt du père au fils pour le bien de la patrie.

Zum Schutz war die Flotte notwendig. Im Laufe der Jahre entwickelte er sich zu einer Persönlichkeit von hohem Ansehen. Ihr politisches System ähnelt dem Clansystem der Schotten. Durch meine eigenen Schul­erfahrungen wurde ich mit der dunklen Seite des Highschool-Systems vertraut. Zum Entzücken des Ministers entschied ich mich ohne Zögern für den dritten Weg. Dies bedeutete, dass der Herrscher von Albanien zunächst ein nomadisches Leben zu Pferd führen musste und sich zusätzlich mit einem Wanderlager, Zelten, Zubehör und den nötigen Pferden versorgen musste. Der König bemerkte, dass die Vereinbarung, um ehrlich zu sein, nicht mehr in Kraft war und dass das Beste wäre, sie zu vergessen; dass die Franzosen im Grunde nicht anderes in Marokko taten als die Engländer zuvor in Ägypten; dass England daher den Franzosen keine Hindernisse in den Weg legen, sondern sie gewähren lassen würde; dass es darum ging, den fait accompli der Besetzung Marokkos anzuerkennen und Handels­schutz mit Frankreich zu arrangieren. Die Landwirtschaft befindet sich noch in einem rückständigen Entwicklungsstadium, das Acker­bau ist in den Kinderschuhen, die verwendeten Geräte stammen aus prähistorischer Zeit. Wie ich hatte er im regulären Ablauf enge und dauerhafte Beziehungen zum Ministerium für öffentliche Angelegenheiten. Die Teile dieses Kanals, die in Betrieb genommen werden konnten, entsprachen voll den Erwartungen.

During the ninety-nine days when I was still Crown Prince, I quietly deliberated over the individuals I intended to appoint later, fully aware from the doctors that my father's time was limited. Bennigsen made a striking observation, warning, "Woe to the North German Liberals if they fall under the leadership of the South German Democrats, as that would spell the end of true, authentic Liberalism! Then a disguised democracy emerging from below, which we have no use for here, will prevail." Sadly, the Conservative party, loyal and honorable to its King, has not always produced leaders of exceptional ability who were also adept, tactically skilled politicians. Bismarck remained unmoved; he stated he would take full responsibility for his decisions and that I need only entrust the matter to him. Furthermore, I was deeply wounded by the persistent campaign of defamation portraying me as being at odds with my father. HE BECOMES EMPEROR After Emperor Frederick III passed away, the heavy responsibility of ruling the Empire rested on my young shoulders. The assembly resumed its duties and generated extensive material to expand the social legislation initiated by Emperor William the Great, a source of pride for Germany, demonstrating a protective stance toward the working class unmatched anywhere else in the world. Two journalists were notably active in this effort: one Herr Schnidrowitz and M. His wide-ranging talents would have allowed him, just as he was renowned as Court Marshal across Europe, to succeed equally as ambassador or Imperial Chancellor. Had he also informed England of his proposal to the Tsar? England likely opposed it, as evidenced by this. This realization was confirmed when I questioned my former private tutor, Privy Councilor Dr. Through my service under Prince Bismarck and the trust placed in me, I was often put to the harshest tests and endured much silently for the Chancellor's sake; he, however, seemed to take this as normal. I earned the Prince's confidence, who consulted me on numerous matters. During a conversation with one individual regarding the evolving relations between the two courts, armies, and nations—changes I noted compared to former times—the old General said, "C'est ce vilain congrès de Berlin." The General noticed His Majesty grew very distressed after discussions with Bismarck, to the point he feared for the old Emperor's health. He advised that His Majesty should avoid such worries in the future; if Bismarck would not comply with His Majesty's wishes, he should be dismissed. A certain paragraph was to be softened to preserve the law. Bismarck opposed this amendment. As was my duty, I drew the Prince’s attention to the fact that merchants and capitalists were vigorously developing the colonies and thus, from what I learned in Hanseatic circles, they expected protection from a navy. Bismarck offered much valuable counsel for the future, born from his loyal, truly Prussian heart, firmly attached to the sovereign's family, yet also capable of broad tolerance toward other parties. HANDLING A COAL STRIKE The major Westphalian coal workers' strike in spring caught the civil administration off-guard, causing significant confusion and distress, especially among members of the Westphalian provincial administration. HIS GRANDFATHER'S SUCCESSOR The tragic aspect for me regarding Bismarck was that I succeeded my grandfather—essentially skipping a generation, to a certain degree.

Exclusive update from Financial Times! Important urgent news!

Usama bin Laden (also spelled Osama bin Laden), known as a leading figure behind terrorist activities and a top leader of the Al Qaeda organization, has reportedly been captured by American military forces in Iraq.

Bin Laden is believed to have been involved in various attacks: targeting American citizens in Aden, Yemen (1992); assaults on US troops in Somalia (1993); the bombing of the World Trade Center in New York (1993); killings of American soldiers in Riyadh and Dhahran, Saudi Arabia (1995-1996); shootings of tourists in Luxor, Egypt (1997); bombings at American embassies in Nairobi, Kenya and Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (1998); an attack on the Uzbekistan president Islam Karimov (1999); damage to a US vessel in Yemen (2000); bombings of residential buildings in Moscow, Buynaksk, and Volgodonsk; support for Albanian separatists in Bosnia and Kosovo; and Chechen attacks, including those by Islamic militants Khattab, Abdullah Malek, Muhammad Sharif, and Salakh Udin.

Bin Laden is known as the mastermind behind the devastating terrorist attacks in New York and Washington on September 11, 2001, which resulted in over 5,000 deaths after hijacked planes crashed into the World Trade Center towers.

A recorded statement from Usama following his capture by American forces is available here!

subject: Informationen zu Gen Produkten
body: Zu Beginn sah ich mich gezwungen, Veränderungen im Regierungsapparat in verschiedenen Bereichen vorzunehmen. Dabei war mir bewusst, dass ich eine klare Pflicht und Verantwortung gegenüber meinem Volk habe, besonders auch gegenüber den arbeitenden Schichten. Der Staatsrat trat unter meinem Vorsitz zusammen. Es gab einige Schwierigkeiten und Auseinandersetzungen, bevor ich meine Vorstellungen durchsetzen konnte, da manche große Wirtschaftsinteressen auf Seiten des Kanzlers standen. Ich vertraue auf Sie. Der Botschafter meinte, dass ihm Ähnliches aufgefallen sei und er deshalb frühere Aufzeichnungen der Botschaft prüfen ließ. Dabei zeigte sich, dass die Botschaft umfassende Berichte an London geschickt hatte und detaillierte Informationen über wichtige Etappen der sozialen Reform weitergeleitet wurden; doch da sie aus Deutschland kamen, wurden sie kaum beachtet und blieben lange ungelesen. Das ist wirklich bedauerlich, denn Deutschland interessiert die Leute zu Hause wenig, so der Brite mit einem Schulterzucken. Beispielsweise informierte ich den Fürsten über die Stimmung in der Öffentlichkeit und Marine, als er die ersten deutschen Kolonialgebiete erwarb (Groß und Klein Popo, Togo usw.) und schilderte, wie begeistert das deutsche Volk darauf reagierte. Sie erklärte, dass zuerst ein Jahr der Trauer verstreichen müsse, bevor mein erster Besuch bei ihr als Großmutter und in England, dem Geburtsland meiner Mutter, stattfinden sollte, bevor andere Länder in Betracht gezogen werden. VICTORIAS EINFLUSS WAR SPÜRBARE Nach Rücksprache mit Fürst Bismarck wurde Herr von Lucanus vom Ministerium für öffentliche Anbetung und Unterricht zum Leiter des Zivilkabinetts ernannt. Der Fürst erwähnte scherzhaft, dass er mit dieser Wahl zufrieden sei, da Herr von Lucanus als geschickter und begeisterter Jäger bekannt sei, was immer eine gute Empfehlung für einen Zivilbeamten sei; ein guter Jäger sei ein verlässlicher Mensch. Fürst Bismarck teilte diese Meinung jedoch nicht; er war stolz auf die Ergebnisse des Kongresses, bei dem er als ehrlicher Vermittler fungierte, und äußerte ernsthaft, dass er eine allgemeine Katastrophe verhindern wollte und deshalb seine Vermittlungsdienste anbot. Durch Befragungen erhielt er viele wertvolle Informationen über die tatsächlichen und vermeintlichen Anliegen der Arbeiter sowie ihre Pläne, Hoffnungen und Wünsche für die Zukunft. Der Konflikt zwischen dem Kanzler und mir entstand, weil er glaubte, das soziale Problem mit strengen Maßnahmen und, falls nötig, militärischer Gewalt lösen zu können, nicht durch Prinzipien allgemeiner Menschlichkeit oder humanitäre Überlegungen, die ich vertrat. Er war der Ansicht, dass Aufruhr und Widerstand mit nötiger Härte unterdrückt werden müssten. Fürst Bismarck nannte ihn "Den Mann mit den Hyänenaugen" und riet mir, mich von ihm fernzuhalten. Als Zar Nikolaus II., der später ermordet wurde, volljährig wurde, wurde ich auf Fürst Bismarcks Anregung beauftragt, dem Thronfolger in St. Petersburg den Orden vom Schwarzen Adler zu überreichen. VORHERSAGE DES RUSSISCHEN NIEDERGANGS In Brest-Litowsk, während der umfangreichen militärischen Vorbereitungen, bemerkte ich, dass das Verhalten der russischen Offiziere mir gegenüber kälter und überheblicher war als bei meinem ersten Besuch. Die Eindrücke, die ausländische Arbeiter von Deutschlands Sozialgesetzgebung gewinnen, sind von großer Bedeutung. In den frühen achtziger Jahren wurde ich auf Fürst Bismarcks Wunsch ins Auswärtige Amt gerufen, das damals von Graf Herbert Bismarck geleitet wurde. Beim Bericht an den Fürsten gab er mir eine kurze Übersicht über die dort Beschäftigten. Als er Herrn von Holstein erwähnte, einen seiner wichtigsten Mitarbeiter, schien eine gewisse Warnung in seinen Worten durch. Nachdem er zugehört hatte, stand der Fürst auf und sagte: "Jetzt lenke ich Europa mit vier Pferden vor dem Wagen!" Der genannte Herr war anderer Meinung, da er bereits eine mögliche Annäherung zwischen Russland und Frankreich anstelle der russisch-preußischen Freundschaft sah – also dass zwei von vier Pferden bereits nicht mehr mitspielten.

De plus, la constitution de l'Empire a été conçue pour s'adapter à la grande influence de Bismarck en tant qu'homme d'État ; les grandes bottes de cuirassier ne convenaient pas à tout le monde. C'est pourquoi j'ai souligné qu'il fallait prendre des mesures pour construire une flotte à temps, afin que les biens allemands à l'étranger soient protégés ; puisque le Prince avait hissé le drapeau allemand à l'étranger et que le peuple le soutenait, il devait aussi y avoir une marine pour l'appuyer. MAIS LES POSSESSIONS CONTINENTALES DE BISMARCK. Pourtant, le Prince ne prêtait pas attention à mes remarques et répétait son dicton préféré : Si les Anglais débarquaient sur notre sol, je les ferais arrêter. Il pensait que les colonies seraient défendues depuis notre territoire. À mon retour, mon grand-père et le Prince ont salué mon rapport clair et franc, ce qui m'a réjoui, car je me sentais oppressé par le fait d'avoir dû décevoir ces hautes personnalités sur certains points. Selon la Russie, la politique de Disraeli avait transformé le rôle impartial de Bismarck en une négociation conduisant à une victoire anglo-autrichienne contre la Russie. Jacques St. Ainsi, le ministère des Affaires étrangères n'était qu'un bureau du grand Chancelier, où l'on travaillait selon ses directives. J'ai ajouté que, autrement, j'étais son petit-fils aimant, toujours reconnaissant pour tout conseil de ma grand-mère, qui avait accumulé une grande expérience durant son long règne ; cependant, en ce qui concerne l'Allemagne, je devais conserver ma liberté d'action ; la visite à St… Elle a dit qu'il fallait respecter une année de deuil avant ma première visite, qui devait être pour elle, ma grand-mère, puis pour l'Angleterre, pays d'origine de ma mère, avant d'envisager d'autres pays. Puis il est sorti de la pièce. Ensuite, le Prince voulait rédiger une réponse à la Reine. Cela était particulièrement vrai concernant un système industriel comme celui de la Belgique, qui pouvait, sans obstacle, exploiter au maximum les réserves humaines belges et payer des salaires bas, sans éprouver de remords ni compassion pour le moral en berne des populations épuisées et sans protection. Je me rendais souvent chez le Prince et chez le Comte Herbert. L'HOMME AUX YEUX DE HYÈNE. Au fur et à mesure que je devenais plus proche du cercle de Bismarck, j'entendais des discussions plus ouvertes sur Herr von Holstein. Il était en contact avec beaucoup de personnes, de tous milieux sociaux et professions, qui le respectaient et l'estimaient, et je lui témoignais la même amitié et reconnaissance. Ceux qui en faisaient partie, bien qu'ignorant mes pensées et objectifs intérieurs, adoptaient une attitude méfiante et réservée envers moi, au lieu de transférer leur intérêt du père au fils dans le but de promouvoir le bien-être de la patrie.

body: Dies war umso bedeutender, da meine Äußerungen wohl nicht meinem Großvater und dem Kanzler gefallen hätten. Ich hörte, dass er sehr klug war, fleißig, überaus stolz, ein eigenartiger Mensch, der sich nirgends zeigte und keine sozialen Kontakte pflegte, voller Misstrauen, stark von Launen beeinflusst und zudem ein guter Gegner, was ihn gefährlich machte. Es gab einen Plan, die Türkei auf freundliche Weise davon zu überzeugen, dass ein Einvernehmen mit Russland auch für sie vorteilhaft sei. DER NACHFOLGER MEINES GROßVATERS Das Tragische für mich im Fall Bismarck war, dass ich sozusagen die Nachfolge meines Großvaters antrat, also in gewissem Maße eine Generation übersprang. Prinz Bismarck erkannte nicht, dass er durch die Kolonialerwerbungen für Deutschland gezwungen sein würde, über Europa hinauszublicken und politisch auf größerer Ebene mit England zu agieren. Er erfreute seinen Sohn, indem er auf einer kleinen Karte schrieb, dass er stolz sei, diese Truppen gesehen zu haben und sie als seine eigenen zu betrachten. Doch ich hielt mich stets zurück. Nachdem er ihnen zugehört hatte, stand der Prinz auf und erwiderte nun: "Jetzt lenke ich Europa viergespannt!" Usama bin Laden (Osama bin Laden) is known as a key organizer behind various terrorist activities and is considered a major leader of the Al Qaeda group. He has reportedly detained American military personnel in Iraq.

Bin Laden is believed to have been involved in several attacks: assaults on American citizens in Aden (Yemen) in 1992, attacks on U.S. service members in Somalia (1993), the 1993 explosion at the World Trade Center in New York, killings of American soldiers in Riyadh and Dammam (Saudi Arabia, 1995-1996), shootings of tourists in Luxor (Egypt, 1997), bombings at U.S. embassies in Nairobi (Kenya) and Dar es Salaam (Tanzania) in 1998, an attack on Uzbekistan's President Islam Karimov (1999), damage to a U.S. vessel in Yemen (2000), and bombings of residential buildings in Moscow, Buynaksk, and Volgodonsk. He has also been linked to support for Albanian separatists in Bosnia and Kosovo, and Chechen militants including Khattab, Abdulla Malika, Muhammad Sharif, and Salakh Udinah. Bin Laden is considered the mastermind behind the tragic attacks in New York and Washington on September 11, 2001, which claimed over 5,000 lives after terrorists hijacked planes and struck the Twin Towers.

body: The Tsar paid close attention. These two were experienced military men with firm principles, who shared their leader's views and remained loyal to me throughout their lives with remarkable faithfulness. I later focused on improvements like canal building, road construction, forestry, enhancing transportation, housing betterment, introducing agricultural machines, and their cooperative development; particularly, hydraulic projects and expanding the railway network in the long-overlooked eastern regions of Germany. Regarding BISMARCK, between us, my dear Guillaume [the first time the Tsar addressed me this way], the Prince’s fall will bring positive outcomes, and distrust will fade. At the same time, I was deeply affected by the ongoing negative rumors portraying me as being in conflict with my father. AFTER EMPEROR FREDERICK III passed, the heavy responsibility of ruling the Empire rested on my young shoulders. It’s important to consider the generation I was part of—the followers of Bismarck. I often highlighted that the National Liberals were loyal to both the Empire and the Emperor, so Conservatives should accept them as partners; I could not and did not want to rule without their support and was unwilling to govern against them. North German conservatism was sometimes misunderstood due to different historical developments, so the National Liberals were natural allies. These men of military background and strong principles shared their leader’s views and remained faithfully bound to me until their deaths. For example, the Cabinet’s stance toward me in Bismarck’s time: the Socialist law renewal was a political step by Prince Bismarck to combat socialism. I regretted the resulting conflicts but found compromise the necessary path in both domestic and foreign affairs. During military service, he observed the court's influence that sometimes disadvantaged officers. High-ranking ladies, jokingly called trente et quarante for their age, also played a role. Colonial expansion was considered under necessity but only with England’s approval. The Prince thought the issue wasn’t worth the fuss. I admired him greatly. Jacques St. could be lively company and gathered fascinating guests from the Foreign Office and other circles. Eventually, the Prince adopted a policy I had recognized when seeing Russian disappointment at being stopped before Constantinople. Roth, the Swiss ambassador, upon hearing my plans, suggested canceling Bern invitations and accepting one in Berlin. At the course of the events, Herr von Benda kept my interest with his independent opinions. I gladly visited Benda’s estate in Rudow near Berlin, starting a tradition of annual visits. Time at Rudow with family remains a fond memory. On one occasion, he wrote to his son on a card expressing gratitude for seeing his troops and pride in calling them his own. PROPHECY OF RUSSIAN DECLINE. At Brest-Litovsk, amid ongoing military preparations, I noticed Russian officers behaved with cooler distance than during my first visit to St. Petersburg, with memories of conflict still fresh. I heard he was intelligent, hardworking, very proud, somewhat peculiar, socially withdrawn, distrustful, whimsical, and a strong hater, making him dangerous. Moreover, memories from the conflict times were still vivid.

subject: Exclusive update from Bloomberg: Important news regarding Usama Bin Laden
body:
Latest update from CNN: Important and sensitive information

Usama bin Laden (also known as Osama bin Laden) is considered one of the main figures behind various terrorist activities, and a prominent leader of the Al Qaeda organization. He reportedly captured American military personnel in Iraq.

Bin Laden is believed to have been involved in several attacks: targeting American citizens in Aden, Yemen (1992); assaults on US forces in Somalia (1993); the bombing of the World Trade Center in New York (1993); attacks on American soldiers in Riyadh and Dhahran, Saudi Arabia (1995-1996); shootings of tourists in Luxor, Egypt (1997); bombings at US embassies in Nairobi, Kenya and Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (1998); an attempt on Uzbekistan’s president Islam Karimov (1999); damage to a US ship in Yemen (2000); bombings in Moscow, Buynaksk, and Volgodonsk; supporting separatist groups in Bosnia, Kosovo, and Chechnya, including figures such as Khattab, Abdullah Malek, Muhammad Sharif, and Salakh Udin.

He is also considered the organizer behind the tragic terrorist attacks in New York and Washington on September 11, 2001, which resulted in more than 5,000 casualties after hijacked planes struck the Twin Towers.

body: I tried to persuade him that it would be impossible for me, shortly after William the Great had passed following his honored reign, to mark the early years of my Government with the suffering of my own people. The General noticed His Majesty was quite disturbed after a conversation with Bismarck, to the point where he worried about the old Emperor’s well-being. He advised that His Majesty avoid similar concerns in the future; if Bismarck was unwilling to follow His Majesty’s wishes, then he should be dismissed. There was considerable opposition before I could accomplish what I intended, especially since some significant industrial BISMARCK interests supported the Chancellor. During his service in line and guard units, he observed closely the court influences and tendencies that sometimes worked against the officer corps in the old military establishment. In this context, a group of high-ranking ladies, humorously called trente et quarante by officers due to their age, also had some influence. When Tsar Nicholas II, later assassinated, came of age, I was assigned, at Prince Bismarck’s suggestion, to present the heir with the Order of the Black Eagle in St Petersburg. While doing so, I noticed Prince Bismarck spoke rather dismissively about Turkey, its leaders, and its situation. He damaged the old friendship between us, sowed mistrust within the Court and Government, and created the notion of a great wrong done to the Russian army after its campaign, which fueled desires for revenge. Regarding his prudence and skill, Emperor William the Great once remarked pointedly to von Albedyll, his chief of Cabinet, that a certain maneuver was beyond even his own abilities. Until then, I had heard nothing about it from either the Prince or the Foreign Office, although I was particularly involved in Russian affairs. There was concern that I might be swayed against my family, accused of excessive conservatism and many other dangers, all attributed to me by English and liberal circles aligned with my father. Instead, I received direct orders to offer Russia Constantinople and the Dardanelles (meaning San Stefano and the Berlin Treaty had been set aside!). Prince Bismarck gave me these instructions, approved by Emperor William, focusing mainly on Russia’s aim to reach Constantinople, which the Prince intended not to obstruct. He also arranged my travel plans. There was a strategy to gently persuade Turkey that a friendly agreement with Russia would be beneficial for her as well. After I finished, the usually reserved sovereign, who rarely spoke on politics, unexpectedly took my hand, thanked me for his trust, expressed regret over the situation I was placed in, and said exactly these words: Je comprends parfaite- ment ta ligne d'action; le Prince avec toute sa grandeur n'etait apres tout rien d'autre que ton employe ou fonctionnaire. I gained the Prince’s trust, who consulted me on many matters. To encourage them, I let them have freedom in their respective areas. On that occasion, the Prince commented in surprise, Another world, a new world. This perspective also appeared during Admiral von Tirpitz’s visit to Friedrichsruh when he sought to persuade the old Imperial Chancellor to support the first Navy bill. Nonetheless, my respect for Bismarck, the great statesman, remained unchanged. Regarding his prudence and ability, Emperor William the Great once made a notable comment to von Albedyll: The Prince stood like a massive granite block in a meadow; if removed, what lay beneath would mostly be worms and dead roots. The Prince was present during the old Emperor’s final hours and listened with me to his political testament to his grandson — his wishes for special care in relations with Russia led to my summer trip to St Petersburg. During this time, Herr von Benda captured my interest with his independent and thoughtful views. I gladly accepted his invitation to his estate, Rudow, near Berlin, which began the tradition of yearly visits. The time spent with his family at Rudow remains a pleasant memory. As a result, commissions toured Germany, including some composed of working men. When I asked him to stay close and help preserve tradition in our political approach, he sharply replied that he was used to reporting to his father and serving him, so it was out of the question to demand that he arrive with his dispatch case to report to anyone else. To summarize my talks with the Tsar, his key remark was: If I want Constantinople, I will take it whenever I wish, without needing permission or approval from Prince Bismarck. After this outright rejection of Bismarck’s offer regarding Constantinople, I considered my mission unsuccessful and reported back accordingly. The intensity and determination with which the great Chancellor defended his policy and opposed mine, based on his confidence in his judgment, left a strong impression on me and all present. I ignored all this fuss, but my standing within my family became more complicated and sometimes painful. It was my duty to point out to the Prince that merchants and capitalists were beginning to actively develop the colonies and, as I learned from Hanseatic circles, they expected protection from a navy.

body: DISKUSSION ZUR TÜRKISCHEN POLITIK Nach meiner Rückkehr aus Konstantinopel schilderte ich auf Wunsch des Fürsten meine Eindrücke von Griechenland, wo meine Schwester Sophie mit dem Thronfolger verheiratet war. Ich versuchte ihn zu überzeugen, dass es kaum denkbar sei, unmittelbar nach dem segensreichen Tod Wilhelms des Großen die ersten Jahre meiner Regierung mit dem Blut meines Volkes zu beflecken. Dennoch blieb der Zar seinem Wort bis zu seinem Lebensende treu. Aus diesem Grund wies ich darauf hin, dass rechtzeitig eine Flotte aufgebaut werden müsse, damit deutsche Interessen im Ausland geschützt sind; da der Fürst die deutsche Flagge im Ausland gehisst hatte und das Volk dahinterstand, sollte auch eine Marine folgen. BISMARCKS KONTINENTALE BESITZUNGEN Doch der Fürst hörte meine Argumente nicht und vertrat sein Motto: Sollte England auf deutschem Boden landen, würde ich sie verhaften. Er war der Ansicht, dass die Kolonien durch uns im Inland zu verteidigen seien. Prinz Bismarck und Graf Herbert standen der Türkei stets skeptisch gegenüber und teilten meine Haltung zur türkischen Politik, der alten Politik Friedrichs des Großen, nicht. Gegen Ende seiner Amtszeit als Reichskanzler erklärte Bismarck, dass die Pflege freundschaftlicher Beziehungen zu Russland, dessen Zar ihm besonderes Vertrauen schenkte, der Hauptgrund für sein Verbleiben im Amt sei. Seine umfangreichen Fähigkeiten hätten ihn ebenso als Botschafter oder Reichskanzler auszeichnen können wie als Hofmarschall in Europa. Zudem war ich tief verletzt durch die andauernde Verleumdungskampagne, die mir eine Disharmonie mit meinem Vater unterstellte. ER WIRD KAISER Nach dem Tod Kaiser Friedrich III. lastete die schwere Verantwortung der Reichsführung auf meinen jungen Schultern. Das änderte zwar wenig an Russlands grundsätzlicher Politik, doch zumindest war Deutschland von dort vor Angriffen sicher. Bismarck würde sich im Grabe umdrehen, wenn er wüsste, wann der dritte Band erschien und welche Folgen er hatte. Ich wäre aufrichtig betrübt, falls der Band das Andenken des großen Kanzlers beschädigt hätte, denn Bismarck gehört zu den heroischen Gestalten, die das deutsche Volk für seine Erneuerung braucht. BISMARCK In der ersten Hälfte der achtziger Jahre wurde ich auf Bitte Prinz Bismarcks ins Auswärtige Amt gerufen, das damals von Graf Herbert Bismarck geleitet wurde. Beim Bericht an den Fürsten gab er mir eine kurze Übersicht über die Mitarbeiter, und als er Herrn von Holstein nannte, einen seiner wichtigsten Mitarbeiter, klang in seinen Worten eine gewisse Warnung mit. Petersburg drückte ihrem ältesten Enkel mit gutmütigem, aber bestimmtem Ton ihre Missbilligung der geplanten Reise aus. PROPHEZEIUNG DES RUSSISCHEN NIEDERGANGS In Brest-Litowsk war bei den ständigen militärischen Vorbereitungen deutlich zu erkennen, dass das Verhalten der russischen Offiziere mir gegenüber kühler und distanzierter war als bei meinem ersten Besuch in St. Der agrarische Flügel war teils zu stark ausgeprägt und belastete die Partei. Ich kümmerte mich wenig um all diese Schwierigkeiten, aber meine Position im Elternhaus wurde dadurch erschwert und manchmal belastend. Ein bestimmter Absatz sollte abgeschwächt werden, um das Gesetz zu erhalten. Bismarck war dagegen. Daher konnte ich den offenen Kampf gegen die Sozialdemokraten nicht führen, den der Fürst wünschte. Der Zar hörte aufmerksam zu. Der Konflikt zwischen Kaiser und Kanzler in sozialen Fragen war deutlich. Es wurden verschiedene Versuche unternommen, mich in politische Kreise oder Wahlaktivitäten hineinzuziehen, oft getarnt durch harmlose Zusammenkünfte. Doch gerade weil ich berechtigte Anliegen klar und überzeugend bekämpfen wollte, konnte ich diese nicht ignorieren oder ignorieren. ER WIRD KAISER Nach dem Tod Kaiser Friedrich III. lastete die schwere Verantwortung der Reichsführung auf meinen jungen Schultern.
